note: Literal upstream case titles and conservative expect-count floors reviewed at pinned source. This gate prevents silently dropping portable cases; it does not prove identical assertion bodies, SQL semantics or server adoption. Source files themselves are not downloaded by CI. HTTP has no dedicated upstream unit suite; its helper assertions are locally derived and upstream entrypoint tests remain a service-owned gap.

portable.title: generates unpredictable-looking tokens and returns stable hashes, never plaintext
requires S256 PKCE with a properly sized verifier, rejects plain or absent PKCE
accepts HTTPS and localhost redirects, rejects insecure external and open redirect forms
does not trust caller-controlled forwarded-for or accept missing IP as a bypass
locks an address after five wrong attempts for fifteen minutes
refuses missing passphrase configuration
requires an exact 32-byte encryption key, without a plaintext fallback
uses AES-256-GCM with unique nonces, context binding, and fails closed on tampering

serverOwned.title: stores a provider-verified test key encrypted; public metadata never contains key
serverOwned.reason: Needs Stripe-owned encrypted key store, account verification and provider fixture.

serverOwned.title: issues encrypted one-time records and returns only a setup link, then consumes once
serverOwned.reason: Service-specific setup route and database mapping; portable adapter tested separately.

portable.title: refuses duplicates across namespaces
refuses tools without a handler

serverOwned.title: registers only the intended safe metadata/audit readers
serverOwned.reason: Asserts Stripe service catalog and write-count not present in generic core.

portable.title: accepts the current registered read tools and properly declared guarded writes
fails when writes is absent or a string, even for harmless-sounding names
fails when a write omits dryRun or confirm, or declares the wrong type
fails money-out tools that lack a provider-derived spec even with confirmation
refuses writes with no trusted lifecycle, and read tools faking a money spec
rejects invalid registry shapes instead of treating them as zero tools

serverOwned.title: actual Stripe write adapter declares money spec only when installed
serverOwned.reason: Stripe lifecycle implementation owns money preparation and actual catalog semantics.

./http.note: No direct upstream HTTP helper suite: local helper behavior tests exercise protocol invariants observed through source OAuth endpoints; case bodies are not claimed to be upstream copies.

portable.title: accepts only configured HTTPS origins, never caller Host headers
writes no-store, nosniff, correct JSON/string responses
HTML-escapes untrusted account names and reflects no markup
parses GET, JSON and form inputs without accepting arrays or invalid bodies
refuses unallowed methods with 405 and Allow header
